HD.rationale: HD presents a mixed picture that lands near neutral. The franchise is structurally strong — unmatched scale, a rapidly expanding Pro ecosystem (SRS, GMS, Mingledorff's) widening TAM to $1.2T, and consistent omnichannel execution. However, the quantitative picture is deteriorating: EPS declined -4.3% YoY despite +4.8% revenue growth, with operating margin compressing from 12.9% to 11.9% (GAAP) and net margin sliding to 8.4%. The P/E at 25.4x has re-expanded ~3 turns from April lows without any earnings inflection — the market is paying the same multiple for lower earnings. The earnings yield of 3.9% sits below the 10-year Treasury at 4.49%, offering no compensation for earnings-decline risk. OCF strength (+39.5% YoY to $6.03B) and equity improvement (+74% YoY) provide a floor, and the sharp crude decline could eventually ease input costs. Comparable sales turning positive for the first time in two years and the ROAD Act legislative tailwind are modest positives. But with cautious FY2026 guidance (flat-to-2% comps, flat-to-+4% EPS), a Wolfe Research downgrade, and Walmart entering the space, the near-term risk/reward is balanced at best. The score reflects a quality franchise in a cyclical trough that is fairly priced — not cheap enough to buy on fundamentals alone, not deteriorating enough to short.
key_factors: EPS declining -4.3% YoY to $3.30 despite +4.8% revenue growth — margin compression at every level (gross margin 33.0% vs 33.8%, GAAP operating margin 11.9% vs 12.9% YoY)
P/E at 25.44x has re-expanded ~3 turns from April 2026 lows (22.4x) without earnings inflection — market paying same multiple for lower earnings
Earnings yield 3.9% below 10-year Treasury yield 4.49% — no compensation for earnings-decline risk in a mature retailer
OCF surged +39.5% YoY to $6.03B, running well above net income ($3.29B) — cash conversion healthy despite earnings decline
Total equity expanded +74% YoY to $13.87B; D/E (total liabilities/equity) improved from 11.5x to 6.8x, though absolute leverage remains elevated
Comparable sales turned positive for first time in two years at +0.6% (U.S. +0.4%); Q1 beat consensus on revenue ($41.77B vs $41.51B) and adjusted EPS ($3.43 vs $3.41)
Pro ecosystem expansion via SRS, GMS, Mingledorff's acquisitions widens TAM to $1.2T; cross-sell synergies targeted at $400M run-rate in 2026
FY2026 guidance cautious: comparable sales flat to +2%, adjusted EPS $14.69–$15.28 (flat to +4%); Wolfe Research downgraded to Peer Perform citing execution risks
WTI crude collapsed from ~$115 to ~$70 (-39%) — potential future margin tailwind not yet reflected in Q1 numbers
ROAD Act passed both chambers with veto-proof majorities — structural housing tailwind, though not yet signed into law
Walmart entering home improvement with exclusive Greenworks Pro power tools line, targeting casual DIY traffic
